Abide

/uh-BYDE/ - rhymes with decide · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Abide means to accept and follow a rule or decision.

Both nations promised to abide by the boundary commission's map, however the line was drawn.

Worked Example

At the county fair, the pie judge's decision cannot be appealed: one blue ribbon, no reasons given. Rosa thought her lattice crust had been robbed, and said so to her sister. Then she pinned the second-place card to her apron, congratulated the winner, and entered again the next summer under the same judge.

Abide is the exact word for what Rosa did, because abide means to accept and follow a rule or decision — you do not have to agree with the call, only to live by it. Accept comes close, but acceptance can stay in your head; abiding by a ruling shows up in what you actually do next.

How Abide Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

honor

honor: to keep faith with a promise or a result — you honor an agreement you made yourself

uphold

uphold: to defend a rule as right; you can uphold a rule that never applied to you

Antonyms

defy

defy: to refuse openly, daring the rule to stop you

violate

violate: to break a rule outright, quietly or not

How Strong Is It? — accept → abide → embrace

accept vs. abide

accept vs. abide: Accepting a ruling can happen entirely in your head — you stop arguing and still change nothing about your plans.

embrace vs. abide

embrace vs. abide: Embrace goes further than abide — an embraced ruling gets defended as if it were your own idea, while abiding by it only requires that you follow it.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — a-

Prefix — a-: on, at — an Old English intensive

Root — bide

Root — bide: to wait, to stay (Old English bidan)

Put it together

Put it together: A- (an Old English intensive, roughly 'on') + bide (to wait, to stay) = to stay on something. In Old English you could abide in a place — stay there — and the word slid from staying put to standing by what has been settled: you stay with the ruling instead of walking away from it.

Use the root in a new word: abode

Use the root in a new word: abode: Her summer abode was a one-room cabin — literally the place where she bides, or stays.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / slightly formal

Abide by is for rules and rulings you follow even when you dislike them — rulings, bylaws, umpires' calls. It is about acceptance, not enthusiasm. Its unit-mates sit nearby: compliant describes meeting written rules, and obedience is doing what a person orders; abide by keeps the focus on a decision you have chosen to live with.
